lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Listen, here's how things stand. The boat, as you can see, is small. It's half-rotten. It leaks in most places. If it tips to one side, over she goes. And you've all turned up at once, each of you hauling a great deal of luggage. If you board with all that, I'm afraid you'll regret it later — especially those of you who can't swim.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: So what do we do to make the crossing?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: I'll tell you. They board naked. All this surplus gets left on the shore. Even then the ferry will barely hold you. And you, Hermes — from here on, your job is to admit no one who isn't stripped clean and has dumped his belongings, as I said. Stand by the gangway, inspect them, and take them on — naked, no exceptions.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Right you are. We'll do it that way. — Now then, who's first?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Menippus, that's me. Look: the satchel and the staff — into the lake with them. The cloak I didn't even bring, which was sensible of me.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Aboard, Menippus, finest of men. Take the seat of honour up by the helmsman, up high — so you can keep an eye on everyone. [pause] And this pretty one — who's he?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Charmoleos of Megara, the heartthrob. His kisses went for two talents apiece.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Strip off the good looks, then. And the lips — kisses included. And the thick hair. And the blush on the cheeks. And the skin, the whole lot. Good. Travelling light. On you go.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And this fellow — the one in purple, with the diadem, the grim face. Who might you be?

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: Lampichus. Tyrant of Gela.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Then why, Lampichus, have you turned up with all this?

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: Well — should a tyrant arrive naked, Hermes?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: A tyrant, no. A corpse, very much yes. So: off with it.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: There. The wealth — thrown away.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And the swagger, Lampichus. Throw that away too. And the superciliousness. They'll weigh down the boat if they come aboard.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: All right — but at least let me keep the diadem. And the cloak.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Absolutely not. Those too.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: Fine. What else? I've dumped everything, as you can see.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And the cruelty. And the stupidity. And the arrogance. And the rage. Dump those too.

lines.speaker: Lampichus
lines.text: [sighs] There. I'm bare.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: On you go. — And you, the fat one, the meaty one. Who are you?

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Damasias. The athlete.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Yes — I thought so. I've seen you often enough at the wrestling grounds.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: That's right, Hermes. So take me aboard — I'm naked.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Not naked, my good man — not with all that flesh wrapped around you. Strip it off. You'll sink the boat the moment you put one foot in. And those victory wreaths — toss them. And the herald's announcements.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: There. Naked, as you see — really naked. Same weight as the other corpses.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Better that way. Unburdened. On board with you. — And you, Craton: put aside the wealth. And the softness, while you're at it. And the luxury. Don't bring the funeral finery either, or the ancestral honours. Leave behind the lineage, the reputation, any public proclamations the city ever made about you, the inscriptions on the statues. And don't mention the enormous tomb they piled up over you — even talking about it adds weight.

lines.speaker: Craton
lines.text: Not willingly. But — I'll throw it away. What else can I do?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Good grief. — And you, the one in armour. What do you want? And what's this trophy you're lugging?

lines.speaker: General
lines.text: Because I won, Hermes. I distinguished myself. The city honoured me.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Leave the trophy up on earth. There's peace in Hades. You won't need any weapons.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And this solemn personage — judging by the get-up, and the strut, and the raised eyebrows, and the thoughtful look, and the long beard hanging down — who is he?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Some philosopher, Hermes. Or rather a fraud, full of mumbo-jumbo. Strip him too. You'll see all sorts of ridiculous things tucked under that cloak.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You — off with the costume first. Then all of this. [pause] Zeus above. Look at the cargo. The pretension he's packing. The ignorance. The quarrelsomeness. The vanity. The unanswerable questions. The thorny arguments. The tangled concepts. And no small amount of pointless effort. And quite a bit of drivel. And nonsense. And pedantry. And — by Zeus — here's some gold. And self-indulgence. And shamelessness. And rage. And luxury. And softness. You didn't fool me, much as you tried to hide it. And put down the lying too. And the conceit. And the conviction that you're better than everyone else. If you boarded with all this, what fifty-oared galley could hold you?

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: Very well. I lay them aside, since you insist.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And that beard, Hermes — make him put it down too. It's heavy, it's shaggy, look at it. Five pounds of hair at the very least.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Good thinking. Off with the beard as well.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: And who's going to do the shearing?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Menippus here. He'll pick up one of the shipwright's axes and chop it off, using the gangway as a block.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No, Hermes — pass me a saw. That'll be funnier.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: The axe will do. [pause] There. Much better. You look more human now you've put down the goat-stink.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Want me to take a little off the eyebrows too?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: By all means. He's got them hoisted halfway up his forehead — for what reason, I can't imagine, the way he keeps lifting himself up. [pause] What's this? Tears, you piece of work? Going weak at the knees in the face of death? Get on board.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: He's still got one thing — the heaviest — under his arm.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: What, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Flattery, Hermes. It served him very well in life.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: Then you too, Menippus — put down the freedom. And the frank speech. And the lack of grief. And the nobility. And the laughter. You're the only one of us laughing.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Don't you dare. Keep them, Menippus. They're light, easy to carry, and useful for the voyage.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And you, the rhetorician — put down all that endless verbiage. The antitheses, the parallels, the periodic sentences, the barbarisms — all the rest of the verbal ballast.

lines.speaker: Rhetorician
lines.text: Look — done.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Excellent. Cast off the lines. Take up the gangway. Haul the anchor. Spread the sail. Steer her straight, ferryman. Smooth sailing.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: What are you wailing about, you fools? Especially you, philosopher — the one we just sheared.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: Because, Hermes, I thought the soul was immortal.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: He's lying. Something else is bothering him.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: What sort of thing?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That he won't be dining on lavish dinners anymore. Or slipping out at night with his head wrapped up in his cloak so no one will recognise him, doing the rounds of the brothels. Or, come morning, swindling young men out of their silver in exchange for wisdom. That's what's bothering him.

lines.speaker: Philosopher
lines.text: And you, Menippus — you're not upset to be dead?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: How could I be? I came running to death, and nobody even called me.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: [pause] But — speaking of which. Isn't that some sort of shouting? People calling from up on earth?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Yes, Menippus. And not from one place either. There are those who've gathered in the assembly and are all laughing happily over Lampichus's death — his wife's being mobbed by the local women, and his children, little as they are, are getting pelted with stones by the other children, plenty of stones. Others are over in Sicyon, applauding the rhetor Diophantus as he delivers a funeral oration for Craton here. And — by Zeus — Damasias's mother is leading the lament, wailing along with the womenfolk over Damasias. But you, Menippus — nobody's shedding a tear. You're laid out in peace, all on your own.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Not for long. You'll hear the dogs howling pitifully over me before long — and the crows beating their wings, when they all gather to bury me.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: A noble man, Menippus. — Well. We've landed. The rest of you, off to the courthouse — straight on, that way. The ferryman and I are off to fetch more.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Smooth sailing, Hermes. — Come along, the rest of us. What are you all waiting around for? We have to be judged — that's certain — and the sentences, they say, are heavy: wheels, stones, vultures. Each man's life will be examined down to the last detail.
